note: Two halves of one form. The band pasodoble: the taurino, militar and festero classics (La Gracia de Dios 1880 to Ragón Falez 1935) in modern recordings by the Banda Sinfónica Municipal de Madrid, the Las Ventas bullring band, La Artística de Buñol and the Villena band for Moros y Cristianos. The sung pasodoble canción: Raquel Meller, Concha Piquer, Estrellita Castro, Celia Gámez, Juanita Reina, Joselito, Lolita Sevilla, Manolo Escobar, Marifé de Triana and Perlita de Huelva. The band recordings are from 1995-2020, not period recordings; no 1920s band 78 was found on a readable page. Ballroom (DanceSport) pasodoble and the Mexican, Puerto Rican and Ecuadorian pasodobles are left out.

size.basis: A judgement, not a count. No source counts pasodoble recordings. What was seen: Spanish Wikipedia says pasodobles are still composed in great numbers on the Levante coast for the Moros y Cristianos festivals, and SGAE found Paquito el chocolatero the most-performed live piece in Spain in 2007; iTunes Spain alone returns dozens of whole albums titled 'Pasodobles', 'Pasodobles Toreros', 'Pasodobles Taurinos' or 'Pasodobles Falleros' by municipal, military and festival bands (Banda Sinfónica Municipal de Madrid, Unidad de Música de la Guardia Real, Banda de la Plaza de Las Ventas, La Artística de Buñol, the Villena bands), each of 10-40 tracks, plus every copla singer of 1930-1970 (Estrellita Castro, Concha Piquer, Juanita Reina, Manolo Escobar) recording sung pasodobles, and compilations such as Warner's 30-track 'Pasodobles' (2020). Counting band repertoire recorded by hundreds of local bands since the 1920s (España cañí was first recorded in 1926) puts the total in the tens of thousands; the low figure counts only distinct commercially issued recordings. An insider's essential list: about 60, roughly 30 band pasodobles (taurino, militar, festero) and 30 sung pasodobles canción.
